message.content:
LeBron James is an American professional basketball player widely regarded as one of the greatest athletes of all time. Born on December 30, 1984, in Akron, Ohio, he rose to prominence as a high‑school phenom at St. Vincent‑St. Mary High School, where he was named the USA Today High School Player of the Year and led his team to a state championship.

He entered the NBA directly from high school in 2003, being selected first overall by the Cleveland Cavaliers. LeBron quickly became a dominant force in the league, earning the NBA Rookie of the Year award in 2004. Over his career, he has played for the Cleveland Cavaliers (two stints), the Miami Heat, and the Los Angeles Lakers.

Key highlights of his career include:

- **NBA Championships**: Four titles (2007 with the Heat, 2012 & 2013 with the Heat, 2020 with the Lakers).
- **MVP Awards**: Four regular‑season MVPs (2009, 2010, 2012, 2013) and one Finals MVP (2012).
- **All‑Star Appearances**: 19 selections (as of 2023), with multiple All‑Star Game MVP awards.
- **Scoring and Playmaking**: He has consistently been among the league’s leaders in points, assists, and rebounds, and he has posted numerous triple‑double seasons.
- **Longevity and Consistency**: LeBron has maintained elite performance into his late 30s, a testament to his conditioning, work ethic, and basketball IQ.

Beyond the court, LeBron is known for his philanthropy, notably the LeBron James Family Foundation, which opened the “I Promise School” in Akron to support at-risk children. He is also a media entrepreneur, producing films and television content through his company SpringHill Entertainment, and he has been involved in various business ventures and endorsements.

In short, LeBron James is not only a basketball legend but also a cultural icon, philanthropist, and business leader whose impact extends far beyond the sport.
